PullRequest.Title: sessions: add tiled session grid infrastructure
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add a reusable tiled layout mode for existing Sessions views without recreating chat widgets
- preserve focus and maximized state while rearranging, and stack tiled sessions in one column on phones
- persist and restore the grid presentation with visible-session state
- keep tiled grids as the leading surface in the single-pane layout

## Context

This extracts the provider-neutral Sessions grid infrastructure needed by #337741 into a small, independently reviewable PR. Once merged, #337741 can merge or rebase this commit and drop its duplicate infrastructure hunks.

Comparison dialogs, tools, controllers, styling, telemetry, provider changes, and Sessions-list affordances intentionally remain in #337741.

## Testing

- `npm run compile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionGridLayout.test.ts src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionsPart.test.ts src/vs/sessions/test/browser/mobileSessionsPart.test.ts src/vs/sessions/test/browser/agentsPartCard.test.ts src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsManagementService.test.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/layout/test/browser/singlePaneStrategies.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new loops, synchronous Grid/SplitView mutation behavior, and SessionView layout call path are directly traceable in repository code. Session counts of 9 and 16 are explicitly covered by the added tests; only the exact duration varies with chat complexity and hardware.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous grid relayouts and repeated SessionView/chat-widget layout work across live DOM views
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For n visible sessions, removing n-1 leaves and adding them back one at a time makes each SplitView mutation synchronously relayout its remaining/current children, producing O(n^2) SessionView layout calls; the tests explicitly exercise grids up to 16 sessions.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Opening or changing a tiled session grid can block the UI thread and visibly jank while all live chat widgets are repeatedly resized before the final topology is reached.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: With the existing columns presentation, updateVisibleSessions only added or removed the delta in slot count; updating the presentation of an unchanged visible set did not remove and re-add all live session views.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Switching to or reshaping tiled mode now tears every existing session view out of the already-laid-out Grid and inserts it again individually. GridView/SplitView performs a synchronous relayout after each removal/addition, and each relayout reaches SessionView.layout and its nested chat layout.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new arrangeSessionGrid implementation adds the reverse loop at lines 16-18 that calls grid.removeView for every leaf except the first, followed by per-leaf grid.addView loops at lines 21-27 and a final distribution. This wholesale structural rewrite did not exist before this PR.
Findings.Title: Batch grid mutations before relaying out session views
Findings.Impact: A realistic 9-16-session grid causes dozens to hundreds of redundant synchronous layouts of heavyweight chat views on the interaction's critical path, delaying the grid's appearance and risking dropped frames; larger accepted arrays increase the cost quadratically.
Findings.Evidence: Grid.removeView reaches SplitView.removeView, which calls relayout(); Grid.addView reaches SplitView.doAddView, which also calls relayout() and, for Sizing.Distribute, distributeViewSizes(). SplitView.layoutViews invokes every current child view's layout, while SessionView.layout immediately resizes its DOM and lays out ChatGroupsView or the standalone chat. The new function performs these mutations in loops and then distributes once more.
Findings.Recommendation: Apply the topology change as one batched grid mutation that suppresses intermediate relayouts, then distribute and lay out once after all existing view elements are placed. Preserve the current view identities, focus, and maximized-state restoration, but avoid invoking SessionView.layout for each intermediate remove/add state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a selected set of existing sessions in the new tiled grid
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The service resolves every requested session, checks whether each unique resolved session may open, and awaits provider preparation before publishing the visible set; publishing then synchronously reconciles SessionView slots and rewrites the Grid topology before the interaction completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/adopt a legacy Copilot CLI session through the agent-host provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one provider-resolution pass per requested input; each actual legacy session can trigger one adoption probe, while non-legacy resources short-circuit synchronously. Calls are serialized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no batched tiled-grid open path; ordinary explicit open resolved only the one session being opened.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every resolution must finish before the visible grid is committed; an actual cold legacy migration probe can therefore block this action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query workspace trust for each folder of each unique resolved session requiring trust
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For each unique trust-gated session, folder trust queries are parallel within that session but sessions are processed serially; already-trusted or non-workspace sessions avoid the checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: An ordinary explicit action checked one session; the new batch path can check every selected unique session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All trust checks and any resulting prompts complete before the grid publishes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare a provider session for open, including connecting a disconnected remote agent host on demand
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One preparation invocation per unique resolved session, serialized. For sessions sharing a remote provider, only the first cold invocation normally establishes the connection and subsequent warm invocations are no-ops.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Ordinary explicit open awaited preparation for one target session; startup restore prepares only the active session asynchronously.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Preparation is awaited before publication; a cold provider connection is on the action's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The requested session array; duplicate resolved resources are coalesced before trust/preparation, but resolution still runs for every input. Added tests cover 9- and 16-session layouts, and the API itself has no count cap.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Resolution, trust checks, and preparation are serialized by the for/await loop. The final observable transaction coalesces publication to one renderer update, but arrangeSessionGrid performs structural mutations sequentially and each mutation relayouts synchronously.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Resolved resources are deduplicated within one call only after resolution. Provider preparation is warm/no-op for already-connected remote providers, while a cold remote provider may connect on the first preparation. There is no cross-call resolution cache, consistent with legacy migration's documented retry semantics.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the serialized service loop, provider implementations, atomic publication, Grid/SplitView relayout behavior, and SessionView layout cascade are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: There is no production caller for openSessionsInGrid in this diff, so boundary latency is latent infrastructure rather than a currently reachable affordance. The synchronous layout mechanism is still concrete for any consumer and its duration depends on live chat complexity and hardware.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous UI regression: the newly added topology rewrite causes O(n^2) repeated live chat layouts. The serialized expensive boundaries were inspected but not separately reported because the API has no production caller in this change and some ordering is required for trust/cancellation semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a previously persisted tiled grid at startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Persisted visible-session states are loaded and resolved by the existing restore flow; the new layout value is committed in the same transaction as restoreGrid, after which the Sessions Part constructs/rebinds slots and arranges the tiled topology once.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and later write the workspace storage snapshot containing visible session states
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One storage read on load and one existing save operation; the diff adds one small layout string per visible entry but no additional storage call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same session-state array was read and written without the gridLayout scalar.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The startup read is pre-existing; the added field only marginally increases parsed bytes. Save is not on grid interaction's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Prepare the active restored session's provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active session, invoked asynchronously; inactive restored slots stay lazy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unchanged: only the active restored session was prepared asynchronously.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the grid-publication critical path by existing design.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of persisted visible session states. The new persisted layout check is one linear scan; rendering scales with restored visible sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing restore flow controls session resolution. Layout and visible state publish atomically, preventing intermediate renderer updates; Grid mutations remain synchronous on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workspace storage is read once into the in-memory ResourceMap. Warm in-memory state avoids additional storage reads. Existing restore behavior prepares only the active provider session asynchronously, leaving inactive sessions lazy.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: transaction boundaries, storage shape, and restore preparation behavior are explicit in code and tests.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Persisted tiled state cannot normally be created by a user-facing caller in this infrastructure-only PR, but it becomes reachable once the service API is consumed. Persisted grid size is not capped.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the reported batched-layout issue. The added linear scan and scalar serialization are negligible, and the transaction avoids intermediate render fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Ordinary session activation/opening and desktop or phone resize
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Active/visible/layout observables drive updateVisibleSessions. Active-only changes rebind already-identical sessions but the new grid shape guard prevents structural rearrangement; resize calls _arrangeGrid, which also returns immediately for an unchanged shape, then performs the normal Grid layout. Phone tiled mode chooses one column only when a shape change is required.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Current visible-session count for reconciliation and normal layout; resize frequency can be high, but shape computation/comparison is constant-time and structural work is skipped when unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All renderer work is synchronous on the UI thread. Observable transactions coalesce related layout/visibility changes; there is no asynchronous boundary in the resize path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: _gridShape is an in-memory positive cache keyed by mode, session count, and derived column count. It suppresses repeated rearrangement on active-state updates and resize; it is updated after successful arrangement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the guard is directly before all structural mutations and both desktop/mobile layout paths call the guarded helper.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normal SessionView layout cost depends on chat content, but this diff does not increase resize cardinality when the shape is stable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression on steady-state activation or resize. The problematic repeated work is limited to shape transitions and is covered by the submitted finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Persist visible session state after grid presentation changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing save path snapshots visible sessions, JSON-serializes the array, and writes it through workspace storage. The diff adds the current layout string to each visible session record.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON-encode visible session state with the added gridLayout property
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional scalar property per visible persisted session within the existing single serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same entries were serialized without gridLayout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: No new save invocation is introduced; only a small linear byte increase to the pre-existing serialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store the serialized active-session state snapshot
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing storage write per save event, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The storage operation already wrote the complete state array.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Call count and placement are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of visible sessions and pre-existing per-session chat state. The added allocation is one repeated two-value string property per visible entry.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialization and storage invocation remain a single synchronous logical save operation; no new fan-out or concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The in-memory ResourceMap remains authoritative between saves; no new cache or retention lifecycle is introduced by the layout scalar.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed object field and unchanged single JSON/store call are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact save frequency is controlled by unchanged lifecycle code, but the incremental bytes are bounded by visible-session count and small compared with existing state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable serialization or I/O regression; the diff adds only bounded metadata without adding calls or pre-cap transformations.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 16 changed files. One medium-severity synchronous layout finding was submitted for per-view remove/add mutations causing quadratic repeated live chat layouts. Provider, trust, persistence, startup restore, resize, cache, and concurrency paths were traced; no other high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
